Privacy Notice

Effective November 25, 2026 · Version 1.1 · Previous versions

What the Screen Gets

  • The items you approve
  • A link to each, which expires

What the Screen Never Gets

  • Your accountNever
  • Your other filesNever

bloop is a new, free side project run by one person in the UK. It keeps only what it needs to put your file on the screen, and deletes a guest's file when the session ends. It never sells data and runs no ads, analytics scripts or trackers. Write to hi@bloop.here about anything here.

This summary helps you read; the full text applies.

1 Who Is Responsible

Summary, not binding: In short: one named person runs bloop and answers for your data.

1.1 bloop is run by Duke DJ Saputra, an individual based in the United Kingdom ("bloop", "we"), as a free side project in early access; it is not a commercial service. bloop is the controller of the personal data described here: it decides why and how that data is used.

1.2 Contact: hi@bloop.here. A postal address is available on request to that address.

1.3 bloop has no data protection officer; none is required. Write to hi@bloop.here.

1.4 Words used here: Screen means a browser showing bloop's page on a shared display, such as a room PC. Session means the time from Approve on your phone until it ends. Item means a file or link you approve for a Screen. Guest File means a file sent from a phone that is not signed in to a file service. Demo means the public sample at bloop.here, which uses a bundled sample account.

2 What Works Today

Summary, not binding: In short: some of what is described here is not live yet, and each part says which.

2.1 bloop is in early access. Rows below marked Planned describe data bloop will handle only once that feature is live. The current list of what is live is on the Security page.

2.2 Today bloop does not connect to Microsoft OneDrive or any other file service. Screens show bloop's sample files and Guest Files.

3 What bloop Collects

Summary, not binding: In short: little, and never the content of your OneDrive.

3.1 The table lists each kind of personal data, where it comes from, and its status.

What bloop collects, where it comes from, and its status
DataFromStatus
A Guest File (its bytes, name, type and size)Fromthe person who sends itStatusLive
A record of each Session: which Item, on which Screen, when, and how it endedFrombloop's own records of what you doStatusLive
A keyed hash of your IP address, used to stop abuse (bloop never stores the address itself)Fromyour browser's connectionStatusLive
Usage counts with no names or file namesFrombloop's own recordsStatusLive
Emails you send to hi@bloop.here, and bloop's repliesFromyouStatusLive
Waitlist answers: your role, where you would use bloop, your organization, what you would like next, your timing and your email, plus the page you came fromFromyou, through the Tally formStatusLive
Your work email and Microsoft account ID (tenant and object ID); never your nameFromMicrosoft, when you sign in and allow accessStatusPlanned
Your OneDrive access, encrypted, and the ID of the folder bloop readsFromMicrosoft, when you sign in and allow accessStatusPlanned
Phone sign-in, as a random value stored only as a hashFrombloopStatusPlanned
A pseudonym (a keyed hash of your account ID) counting weekly active usersFrombloopStatusPlanned

3.2 bloop never stores the content of files from your OneDrive. It fetches a file only when you approve it, and passes it to the Screen. A Guest File is the one exception, and it is deleted when the Session ends (section 5).

3.3 bloop does not use your data for automated decisions about you, and does not build profiles.

3.4 Photos sent as a Guest File are re-encoded on your phone before they leave it, which removes their location and other metadata. Videos have their location fields cleared on your phone. Some cameras also write location in other places, such as an XMP block or a GPS track, which bloop does not clear; send a video you are content to show.

4 Why bloop Uses It

Summary, not binding: In short: to run the Session you start, keep it safe, and answer you.

4.1 Each purpose and its lawful basis under the UK GDPR:

Each purpose, the data it uses, and its lawful basis
PurposeDataLawful basis
Put the Items you approve on the Screen you chooseDataSession records, Guest Files, OneDrive access (Planned)Lawful basisContract: providing the service you ask for
Show a Guest File on the Screen its sender choseDatathe Guest FileLawful basisLegitimate interests: showing the file the sender picked, for the time they picked
Stop abuse and keep the service safeDataIP hash, Session recordsLawful basisLegitimate interests: security and fraud prevention
Give your organization's IT team a record of what was opened whereDataSession recordsLawful basisLegitimate interests: accountability on shared machines; under an agreement with your organization, bloop acts on its instructions instead
Count use, with no names, to improve bloopDatausage counts, weekly pseudonyms (Planned)Lawful basisLegitimate interests: improving the service
Invite you to early access and arrange a callDatawaitlist answersLawful basisConsent, which you can withdraw at any time
Answer your emailsDatayour emailsLawful basisLegitimate interests: replying to you

4.2 You have the right to object at any time to any use based on legitimate interests. Write to hi@bloop.here and bloop will stop unless it has compelling grounds that override your interests, or needs the data for a legal claim.

5 How Long bloop Keeps It

Summary, not binding: In short: a guest's file goes when the Session ends; records go on a fixed clock.

5.1 A daily job deletes data when its period ends. Data and Retention explains each period.

6 Who Helps Run bloop

Summary, not binding: In short: three companies process data for bloop, and none may use it for themselves.

6.1 These processors handle personal data only on bloop's instructions, under written terms:

The processors, what each does, the data it handles and where

6.2 Microsoft is not a processor for bloop. When OneDrive is live, Microsoft is where your files and sign-in come from, and it controls your Microsoft account under its own terms and your organization's.

6.3 bloop does not sell personal data, and shares it with no one else except where the law requires it.

7 Where Data Is Stored

Summary, not binding: In short: stored in the EU, run by a US company, with legal safeguards.

7.1 bloop's database and Guest Files are stored in the EU. bloop never claims "UK only": Cloudflare is a US company, and a request is handled at the Cloudflare data center nearest the person making it.

7.2 Where data goes outside the UK, the safeguards are the UK's adequacy regulations for the EU, and for the US the EU Standard Contractual Clauses with the UK Addendum in Cloudflare's data processing terms. Tally's and Apple's transfers follow their own published terms.

9 Your Rights

Summary, not binding: In short: ask to see, fix, move or delete your data; bloop answers within a month.

9.1 You have the right to:

  1. (a) get a copy of your data (access);
  2. (b) have it corrected;
  3. (c) have it erased;
  4. (d) restrict how it is used;
  5. (e) receive it in a portable format;
  6. (f) object, as in 4.2;
  7. (g) withdraw consent to the waitlist at any time, without affecting what came before.

9.2 Write to hi@bloop.here. bloop replies within one month, and may ask you to prove who you are first. In some cases the law allows a longer time or a refusal; bloop will say why.

9.3 Once OneDrive is connected, tap Disconnect OneDrive on any phone while you approve: bloop deletes its stored access and every sign-in ends at once, a lost phone's included. You may also be able to remove bloop in My Apps (myapplications.microsoft.com); your IT team can remove it for everyone in Microsoft Entra.

10 How to Complain

Summary, not binding: In short: tell bloop first; you can always go to the ICO.

10.1 To complain about how bloop uses your data, write to hi@bloop.here with "Complaint" in the subject. bloop acknowledges a complaint within 30 days, looks into it without undue delay, and tells you the outcome.

10.2 You may also complain to the Information Commissioner's Office (ICO), the UK regulator, at any time, at ico.org.uk/make-a-complaint, which lists its helpline and postal address. The ICO usually expects you to raise it with bloop first.

11 Children

Summary, not binding: In short: bloop is for work and study, and not for children under 13.

11.1 bloop is made for staff and students at universities, schools and workplaces. It is not meant for children under 13, and bloop does not knowingly collect their data. A Guest File, from anyone, is deleted when its Session ends.

12 Changes to This Notice

Summary, not binding: In short: changes are dated and listed here.

12.1 bloop will post any change here with a new version and date. For a material change, bloop will email people on the waitlist and, once sign-in is live, signed-in users, before it takes effect.
